title: Batch 5 text-roman lane: Rome 1604 and Rome 1635 Canon constituents, exact 1604 witness, Rome 1634 search

uses.finding: Added the exact Rome Typographia Vaticana 1604 copy (National Central Library of Rome, Internet Archive bub_gb_aaPpAuHRY9IC) as candidate roman-1604-rome-vatican-bncr-aappauhry9ic and as the witness of roman-stages-1604; title, Cum sanctissimum (dated 7 July 1604) and the complete Canon (printed pp. 251-254) were read on the original images. The Canon of the Rome Vatican 1635 Urbanian printing (Google XNC4a07qPqQC, printed pp. 245-249) was read likewise. Both Canons are transcribed as bounded native constituents (17 units each) with retained page images. Checked on the images of all three books, the 1604 Canon against Rome 1570 prints N. et N. in the Memento of the living, Amen after the Communicantes and Hanc igitur conclusions, Iungit manus before the Memento of the dead conclusion, and reorders the chalice elevation after a secret Haec quotiescumque, with further rubric changes; against 1604 the 1635 Canon adds only the head bow 'Iungit manus, et caput inclinat' at the end of the Memento of the dead. [Cold review: the lane's further claims Et quotquot to ut quotquot, a reordered doxology and an added Amen after the Memento of the dead rested on misreadings in the roman-1570-canon-missae reading and were removed.]
uses.limit: Both readings were independently collated and activated on 2026-10-22; one copy per edition. No whole-book collation; orthography, capitalization and punctuation differences are not counted as changes. The roman-1570-canon-missae reading needs re-collation before its wording is diffed.
uses.next_sources: Re-collation of the roman-1570-canon-missae reading against its images; Ordo Missae (before the Canon) for 1570, 1604 and 1635; a 1634-dated Rome issue, if any.

uses.finding: Owned route not changed. The 1474 Milan stage remains witnessed only through Lippe's 1899 critical edition; no digitized copy of the 1474 incunable itself was sought in this lane, so no 1474 Canon binding was attempted (the coordinator ranked it last).
uses.limit: A 1474 binding needs the exact incunable, not Lippe.
uses.next_sources: Digitized copies of the Milan 1474 Missale Romanum (ISTC census) for a Canon constituent.

limits: Every Canon word was read on the page images; provider OCR only located pages. The readings share the letter-form conventions of the Rome 1570 Canon reading (orthographic regularization, accents omitted) but keep printed capitalization and punctuation, so they are not diplomatic. Transition changes compare single copies and claim no first introduction. HathiTrust and Gallica refused access (403); SBN OPAC returned no machine-readable list.

independent_review.reviewer: independent batch-5 cold reviewer, distinct from the lane author and the coordinator
independent_review.scope: Read on the original page images, independently of the lane: every line of both new Canon readings (Rome 1604 IA leaves 0348-0351; Rome 1635 Google PA245-PA249), the 1604 title and Cum sanctissimum (including its dating clause die vij. Iulij MDCIIII) and the 1635 title, Cum sanctissimum, Si quid est and colophon; re-fetched three images per book from the source URLs (byte-identical) and matched every PDF page to its package member. Every transition claim was checked on the images of the books on both sides, including the retained Rome 1570 Canon openings 169-172. Corrections: two 1635 punctuation readings; three 1570->1604 anaphora sub-claims removed or narrowed because they rested on misreadings in the activated roman-1570-canon-missae reading rather than on its print (Ut quotquot, et in ipso before the doxology rubric, Amen already printed after the Memento of the dead); normalization wording narrowed (the 1570 reading does not keep printed capitals); a contradiction in the Urbanian transition text removed; gap evidence narrowed. Both native books were then activated. The 1570 reading itself was not corrected and needs re-collation. The IA 1630-1640 search was re-run (3 hits, no Rome 1634); the Google feed, HathiTrust, Gallica and SBN searches were not re-run. No body text outside the strict Canon was collated.
